```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", width = 88)
library(readNBS)
```

`readNBS` is for analysts who need selected official National Bureau of
Statistics of China (NBS) series and release tables while retaining the
published reporting geometry and source provenance. The package's supported
identity is a stable semantic series or dataset ID. Portal UUIDs and request
paths are transport details held behind local manifests.

This article leads from local discovery through deterministic retrieval and a
complete time-series chart, then shows where an explicit live request belongs
in an analysis. Package checks execute the local examples from retained data
or injected transports; the live section runs only in an interactive session.

## Find a series locally

The bundled scalar catalogue and search index provide local discovery:

```{r search}
cpi_hits <- nbs_search("CPI", limit = 5L)
cpi_hits[c("series_id", "title", "frequency", "unit", "route")]
```

The result is a base `data.frame`. Save `series_id` as the semantic identity;
portal UUIDs remain transport details managed by the manifest.
`nbs_catalogue()` returns the same semantic
metadata without the search filter, and `nbs_manifest()` exposes the
time-bounded UUID mappings and source notes used by the retrieval layer.

## Retrieve and chart a time series

The package includes versioned, retained official seasonally adjusted revision
histories. This workflow discovers three comparable month-on-month series,
fetches them through `nbs_fetch_series()`, and charts the public output
contract. Retrieval is fully offline. The complete returned rows retain their
source and vintage fields; the chart keeps only the three columns it needs.

```{r chart-discovery}
month_on_month <- nbs_search("month-on-month", limit = 50L)
selected_ids <- c(
  "NBS/CN/M/FAI/TOTAL/MOM_PERCENT_OFFICIAL_SA",
  "NBS/CN/M/INDUSTRY/VALUE_ADDED/MOM_PERCENT_OFFICIAL_SA",
  "NBS/CN/M/RETAIL/TOTAL/MOM_PERCENT_OFFICIAL_SA"
)
series_ids <- selected_ids[selected_ids %in% month_on_month$series_id]
stopifnot(identical(series_ids, selected_ids))

month_on_month[
  match(series_ids, month_on_month$series_id),
  c(
    "series_id", "title", "frequency", "unit", "available_from",
    "available_to", "route"
  ),
  drop = FALSE
]
```

The two coverage columns define the supported retrieval window for each exact
identity. `available_to = NA` denotes an open-ended route, while a date marks a
bounded retained history or classification era. See the [Data coverage
article](data-coverage.html) for the complete subject-family map and
dimensional-dataset inventory.

The retained routes are package data. A strict injected client makes the
offline boundary visible, while the ordinary parser validates and combines
the official snapshots. Base R keeps the chart columns, removes non-finite
values, and trims the repeated title suffix for concise legend labels.

The three histories are the exact IDs shown above. Their installed
`nbs-fai-sa-history-release-index.csv`,
`nbs-industry-sa-history-release-index.csv`, and
`nbs-retail-sa-history-release-index.csv` files record the official NBS source
URLs and capture hashes for the normalized retained histories.

```{r chart-fetch}
chart_client <- nbs_client(
  transport = function(...) stop("The chart example attempted a network request."),
  retries = 0L,
  now = function() as.POSIXct("2026-07-29 12:00:00", tz = "UTC")
)

chart_data <- do.call(rbind, lapply(series_ids, function(series_id) {
  observations <- nbs_fetch_series(
    series_id,
    start = "2024-01",
    end = "2025-05",
    client = chart_client
  )
  observations[c("date", "value", "title")]
}))

chart_data <- chart_data[is.finite(chart_data$value), , drop = FALSE]
chart_data$series <- sub(" month-on-month$", "", chart_data$title)
utils::head(chart_data[c("date", "value", "series")], 3L)
```

The plot maps the package's real `date` and `value` columns and a concise
series label derived from the returned `title`. `ggplot2` is optional; when
available it renders the figure during vignette and pkgdown builds.

```{r time-series-chart, fig.width=8, fig.height=4.8, out.width="100%", fig.alt="Line chart comparing monthly percent changes in fixed-asset investment, industrial value added, and retail sales from January 2024 to May 2025."}
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  ggplot2::ggplot(
    chart_data,
    ggplot2::aes(x = date, y = value, colour = series, group = series)
  ) +
    ggplot2::geom_line() +
    ggplot2::labs(
      title = "Selected official NBS month-on-month series",
      subtitle = "Monthly published observations",
      x = "Month",
      y = "Percent",
      colour = "Series",
      caption = "Source: National Bureau of Statistics of China."
    ) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
}
```

The README uses the same IDs, dates, series labels, and attribution so the
GitHub home page and this article stay aligned.

## Fetch a fixture-backed current observation

The installed `inst/extdata/examples/cpi-2026-june.json` file is a small,
source-attributed NBS response snapshot. An injected transport lets the
ordinary parser exercise the frozen response deterministically:

```{r fixture-fetch}
fixture_path <- system.file(
  "extdata", "examples", "cpi-2026-june.json", package = "readNBS"
)
stopifnot(nzchar(fixture_path), file.exists(fixture_path))
fixture_body <- paste(
  readLines(fixture_path, warn = FALSE, encoding = "UTF-8"),
  collapse = "\n"
)

fixture_transport <- function(request) {
  if (!identical(request$body$dts[[1L]], "202606MM-202606MM")) {
    stop("The fixture only covers June 2026.")
  }
  list(
    status = 200L,
    headers = list(`content-type` = "application/json"),
    body = fixture_body
  )
}

client <- nbs_client(
  transport = fixture_transport,
  retries = 0L,
  now = function() as.POSIXct("2026-07-29 12:00:00", tz = "UTC")
)

cpi <- nbs_fetch_series(
  "NBS/CN/M/CPI/HEADLINE/YOY_INDEX",
  start = "2026-06",
  end = "2026-06",
  client = client
)
cpi[c("period", "value", "raw_value", "unit", "source_vintage")]
```

The value is an index whose same-month-previous-year base is 100. It is not a
percentage until the explicit conversion helper is applied. The returned
frame also carries `source_url`, `raw_sha256`, `manifest_version`, and the
reporting-period fields needed to audit the observation.

## Read a retained official revision history

Some official seasonally adjusted revision histories are bundled as retained
source snapshots. They are useful for a fast first success even when no
transport fixture is needed:

```{r retained-history}
offline <- nbs_client(
  transport = function(...) stop("This retained example attempted a network request."),
  retries = 0L,
  now = function() as.POSIXct("2026-07-29 12:00:00", tz = "UTC")
)

activity <- nbs_fetch_series(
  "NBS/CN/M/INDUSTRY/VALUE_ADDED/MOM_PERCENT_OFFICIAL_SA",
  start = "2025-04",
  end = "2025-05",
  client = offline
)
activity[c("period", "value", "source_vintage", "route")]
```

`route` and `source_vintage` distinguish retained revision snapshots from
latest/revised portal data. A complete retained range runs entirely offline.

## Fetch current portal data explicitly

The default client uses the official HTTPS portal, bounded per-attempt
timeouts, bounded retries, and an in-memory cache owned by that client. Public
NBS routes use anonymous access. This article keeps the live call explicit:

```{r live-request, eval=TRUE}
if (interactive()) {
  live_cpi <- nbs_fetch_series(
    "NBS/CN/M/CPI/HEADLINE/YOY_INDEX",
    start = "2025-01",
    end = "2025-12",
    client = nbs_client(timeout = 15, retries = 2L)
  )
  head(live_cpi[c("period", "value", "source_vintage")])
}
```

Installation and startup are local operations. A portal fetch may read or
populate the client's bounded response cache, which can be cleared with
`nbs_clear_cache(client)`. Cache entries stay in memory and belong to one
client.

## What to read next

* [Dimensional datasets](dimensional-datasets.html) explains dependent
  dimensions, valid tuples, and panel retrieval.
* [Data coverage](data-coverage.html) maps the supported series families,
  historical starting points, finite archives, and open-ended routes.
* [Provenance and reporting calendars](provenance-reporting-calendars.html)
  shows how to preserve source vintages and treat cumulative reporting
  windows explicitly.
* [Troubleshooting and live maintenance](troubleshooting-live-maintenance.html)
  covers changed routes, fixture-driven checks, and the intentionally separate
  Yearbook maintenance path.

The package is currently distributed as a GitHub development release, and the
public portal's route contract can evolve. Keep the package version, stable
ID, requested period, source URL, and provenance fields with any downstream
result, and check the [NBS attribution
terms](https://www.stats.gov.cn/english/nbs/200701/t20070104_59236.html) when
quoting or redistributing data.
